clue.text: It heralds delivery — of a kiss?

definitions.text: It heralds delivery — of a kiss?

parts.words: It heralds delivery — of a kiss?
parts.note: literally the rap at the door before letters arrive; also the name of a party game in which a kiss is the 'letter' delivered

explanation.surface: Something announcing a delivery, though the delivery here may be a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is the sound at the door when the post comes; the question mark points to the British party game where players pay for a pretend letter with a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: The rap a letter carrier gives on the door announces mail, and the same name belongs to a kissing game at parties.

clue.text: Sweetmeat distributed in packet to France

indicators.note: distributed means the letters of the following words are spread about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sweet being handed out from a parcel sent to France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' is the anagram signal and 'in' just links. The answer is a small round liquorice sweet from the Yorkshire town of Pontefract.
explanation.definitionFit: This small liquorice disc is a traditional British confection, and sweetmeat is an old word for any sweet.

clue.text: Channel showing "Sister Susie", perhaps

explanation.surface: A broadcast channel airing a programme called Sister Susie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sister Susie's Sewing Shirts for Soldiers' is a First World War music-hall song, so Sister Susie is one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A drain is an underground channel for waste, and someone who stitches clothes, like the Susie of the old song, is a needleworker by that spelling too.

clue.text: I'm not in USA, strangely; I'm in Egypt

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the preceding words are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone protesting that they are not in America at all but in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges IMNOTINUSA. The definition speaks as the mountain itself: the peak of Exodus lies in Egypt's Sinai peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical mountain stands in the Sinai peninsula, part of Egypt, so it can say of itself that it is there.

clue.text: The stuff to make girl enthusiastic

parts.note: Nan is a girl's name, short for Ann or Nancy
keen means eager or enthusiastic

explanation.surface: Advice on the right thing to get a girl excited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The stuff' looks like 'the right thing'; it means a fabric. Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally from Nanjing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for woven fabric, and this is a buff cotton cloth.

clue.text: Unprincipled, like Jack

explanation.surface: A dishonest person compared to someone called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: In a pack of cards the jack is also called the knave.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest or roguish describes the first sense, and the second means resembling the jack in playing cards, otherwise the knave.

clue.text: Seconds out of Rugby revels!

annotationWithheld.why: Seconds out of Rugby revels! (4) for ORGY: 'revels' defines it, but no reading of 'Seconds out of Rugby' gives ORGY (removing the second and fourth letters of RUGBY leaves RGY, with nothing to supply the O); scan and search confirm the text

clue.text: Creature giving man firm support

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess, and the king is one
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: Something that gives a man solid support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' here is a chess piece, the king; 'giving' links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A large venomous Asian snake, an animal and so a creature.

clue.text: Soldiers advanced, without head displaying implacability

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to advance money is to lend it, past tense lent
less means lacking or without
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Troops pushing forward without a leader showing no mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without head' reads as 'leaderless', but each word gives its own piece: LESS and NESS, the headland found in names like Loch Ness's neighbours and Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unstoppable and unyielding is the quality of something that cannot be appeased.

clue.text: Island worth £1.05?

parts.note: a guinea was twenty-one shillings, which after decimal currency arrived equals one pound five pence, so a modern guinea would be worth that

explanation.surface: Asking which island could be bought for a pound and five pence.
explanation.walkthrough: The guinea was an old British coin of 21 shillings; in decimal money that is £1.05, so a guinea in new money suggests the large Pacific island.
explanation.definitionFit: The large island north of Australia has a name that sounds like a modern version of the old coin worth that sum.

clue.text: Information about style

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Some facts concerning fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for the facts on something.
explanation.definitionFit: A category of art or writing is a kind or manner, a style.

clue.text: Bird runs off to grieve

indicators.note: off means the letter for runs is taken away from the word for grieve

parts.note: to regret is to feel sorrow, to grieve
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A bird flies off to mourn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs off' looks like the bird leaving; it means R comes off REGRET.
explanation.definitionFit: A white heron, one of the wading birds.

clue.text: Verse about a ruler

indicators.note: about means the word for verse is turned round

parts.note: rime is an old spelling of rhyme, verse

explanation.surface: A poem written about a sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning'; here it turns RIME round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim prince or governor, a ruler in the Middle East.

clue.text: 100 square metres, about 100 square yards

indicators.note: about means the word for 100 square metres goes round the Roman numeral

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, 100 square metres
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A conversion between metric and imperial measures of land.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a conversion table; the second 100 is the Roman C. The definition is loose: the answer is 4,840 square yards.
explanation.definitionFit: An imperial unit of land area of 4,840 square yards, so a measure counted in that unit.

clue.text: Club in Peel wound up by censor

indicators.note: wound up suggests the letters are twisted round into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A club is injured in Peel and blamed on the official censor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound up' rearranges CLUBINPEEL; 'by' links. Peel is a town on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue-pencil is to cut or edit out text, as a censor does with a coloured pencil.

clue.text: Raced round naval vessel, one from overseas

indicators.note: round says the word for raced goes about the ship and the one

parts.note: ran means raced
USS prefixes the name of a United States Navy ship
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone sped around a warship, a foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts the ship and the one inside the word for raced. USS stands for United States Ship. The definition 'from overseas' is loose and uses the answer as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The defining phrase is loose: a native of a distant country such as Russia comes from abroad.

clue.text: Several lived outside the hospital, in an unspecified place

parts.note: some means several

indicators.note: outside means the word for lived goes around the hospital letter

parts.note: were means existed, lived
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Several people lived outside the hospital, somewhere unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the verb round the hospital letter. 'lived' stands for 'were' in the sense of 'existed', which is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb for at a location not named or known.

clue.text: Henry I had an objection to fish

parts.note: Hal is a pet form of Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal
a but is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: King Henry I complained about a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry I' looks like the king; it is HAL plus I. 'had an' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flatfish of northern seas.

clue.text: The range of underwear worn by fathers

indicators.note: worn by places the word for fathers inside the word for underwear, as a garment wraps its wearer

parts.note: coms is short for combinations, an old one-piece undergarment
pas are fathers, daddies

explanation.surface: The range of underwear that fathers wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn by' puts the fathers inside the underwear, the way a garment wraps the person wearing it. Combinations are old-fashioned one-piece long underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass means extent or scope, the range of something.

clue.text: Second auditor employed in the wool business

parts.note: an auditor in its original sense is a listener, a hearer

explanation.surface: A second accountant hired by a wool company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' tempts as an accountant; it means a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep-clipper works in wool production, cutting fleece from sheep.

clue.text: Make about a thousand burn

indicators.note: about means the word for make goes round the thousand

parts.note: to create is to make
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Earn around a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make about a thousand' reads like earning roughly £1,000; CREATE goes round M.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce a body to ashes by fire.

clue.text: Sharp, some say, and swift creature

indicators.note: some say means the word for a sharp is heard rather than read

parts.note: a sharp, as in card-sharp, is a swindler or cheater

explanation.surface: A sharp, fast animal, so people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp' looks like an adjective; it is a noun, a swindler. In a non-rhotic British accent the word for one sounds like the big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted big cat is the fastest land animal.

clue.text: Neat town, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the town's name is heard as a different word

parts.note: Cowes is a town on the Isle of Wight, famous for sailing

explanation.surface: A tidy town, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy; it is an old word for cattle. COWES is a yachting town on the Isle of Wight.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic word for cattle, bovine animals.

clue.text: Just water

explanation.surface: Nothing but water.
explanation.definitionFit: Just means only or nothing more than, and the second sense is a small lake or pond.

clue.text: English birds, and where they may nest

parts.note: Aves is the Latin name for the class of birds

explanation.surface: English birds and their nesting places.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition's 'they' refers back to the birds of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds such as swallows and martins build nests under the overhanging edge of a roof.

clue.text: Heaven used to contain a goddess

indicators.note: to contain says the answer is held within the words Heaven used

explanation.surface: Heaven was once home to a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to' reads as 'formerly'; 'to contain' signals the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman goddess of love.

clue.text: Map — one mislaid by guide

indicators.note: mislaid by means the guide has lost the letter for one

parts.note: a pilot is a guide, especially one steering ships into port
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A map, one lost by a tour guide.
explanation.walkthrough: PILOT loses I.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a plan or chart of an area, a map.

clue.text: Tolling of the bell the Dickensian heroine heard

indicators.note: heard means the heroine's name is taken as a spoken sound

parts.note: Little Nell is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop

explanation.surface: Dickens's heroine hears a bell tolling.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent K means the heroine's name and the bell's sound are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow ringing of a bell, especially at a funeral.

clue.text: Centre abroad holds diamonds in reserve

indicators.note: holds means the jumbled letters of centre go around the diamonds
abroad means scattered widely, so the letters of centre are moved about

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A foreign centre keeps diamonds in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges the letters of the first word into RETNCE, and 'holds' puts the diamonds inside that. 'in' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve as restraint in speech: a reluctance to say much.

clue.text: Settler — he isn't disposed to engage in controversy

indicators.note: disposed means arranged or set out, so the letters are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: A settler who is not inclined to argue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' looks like 'inclined'; it rearranges SETTLERHEISNT. The phrase comes from knights entering the jousting enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: To join a contest or debate, from riding into the jousting ground.
